title: Orbital rescue
evidenceStatus: Frozen main 4c0c40d5; six decoded episodes on three seeds; 192 transitions replayed; independent route oracle and 1,000 code-only seeds; no browser or model calls
summary: Both controllers win all three published seeds, but none of the six trajectories offers an immediate hazardous or out-of-bounds choice. Jev matches the code greedy rule on 95 of 96 moves with code-selected objectives and supplied distances. Live mission state waits for model answers, and controller switching restarts the mission, so real-time shared play needs a separate clock and ownership design.
strengths: All 192 published transitions and final states replay exactly in the deterministic engine; a genuine win requires all cores and return to the beacon.
Matched-seed Jev/greedy records, explicit fixed-clock replay labeling, visible observations and probabilities make the decision boundary inspectable.
Manual keyboard/button controls, WebGL fallback, reduced-motion rendering, resource disposal and reset/unmount request invalidation already exist.

findings.title: The recorded trajectories never test immediate hazard avoidance
findings.evidence: probes/orbital.json: six episodes, zero unsafe alternatives, 95/96 Jev-greedy agreement; seed 42 takes 30 moves versus exact no-damage optimum 26. engine.ts:153 supplies a selected goal and :168 supplies action distances. Code-only seeds 0..999 all win with greedy; 26 have duplicate hazards from engine.ts:86.
findings.impact: The evidence supports easy assisted geometric action selection, not robust rescue planning. A crafted state makes greedy time out despite a verified 10-move safe route; Jev was not called on that state.
findings.fix: Enforce distinct hazards, freeze solvable detour and route-order cases, compare an independent route oracle, and separate geometry-only observations from objective/preview assistance.

findings.title: Model response time controls the world clock and modes cannot hand off
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/arcade.tsx:261 RAF only renders; :379 awaits a response before :414 advances state; :424 schedules the next request afterward. :446 resets on mode switch. :548 Pause leaves the pending generation valid.
findings.impact: Latency freezes mission progress, switching controllers loses the current run, and one pending move can apply after Pause. These are source-level lifecycle findings.
findings.fix: Add an independent simulation clock, explicit controller ownership, deadline/revision guards, bounded goal execution, visible fallback, same-state takeover and checkpoint branch generations. Define game pause separately from suspending model control.

findings.title: Docking and navigation need visible coordinates that match the rules
findings.evidence: arcade.tsx:168 places the beacon ring at y=0.05; engine.ts:228 requires y=2. Probe verifies y=0 remains playing and y=2 wins. Camera orbit at :127 does not change absolute keyboard axes at :492; the main HUD lacks compass/altitude. Collision uses center distance below 0.8, while the renderer draws separate rotor geometry.
findings.impact: Humans must infer decisive altitude and world directions that the model receives explicitly. Visible flight geometry does not define the grid collision rule.
findings.fix: Place a target marker at the actual dock, show compass and current/target altitude, offer a top-down inset and display the grid collision proxy. Version any future continuous collider rules.

findings.title: Action budget, oxygen and full-game progression need separate definitions
findings.evidence: engine.ts:164 and :231 give 70 actions and an oxygen timeout; idle time costs nothing. arcade.tsx:507 shows moves but no remaining resource; only three seed choices and restart exist.
findings.impact: The finite mission is winnable, but its resource wording implies time pressure it does not implement. The experience ends after one mission without progression or recovery choices.
findings.fix: Keep the legacy 70-action task versioned, show its remaining maneuver budget, and define actual oxygen/fuel separately in play. Add a complete short campaign and report evaluation truncation independently from game loss.

findings.title: Recorded request time is copied batch service latency
findings.evidence: record.ts:71 copies one response.service_latency_ms and :73 total batch cost into every pending game's action; arcade.tsx:623 labels it Request time. Orbital median/p95/max are 318/428/1011 ms across 96 decisions, with physical requests not identifiable.
findings.impact: These rows cannot establish independent request latency, retry availability or total cost by summation, and they differ from live wall timing.
findings.fix: Label legacy service timing accurately and add a physical-request ledger with IDs, retries, wall/service time and cost, plus decision application tick and deadline outcomes.

simulation.title: A rescue sortie with shared controls
simulation.description: A versioned three-mission real-time game teaches flight and docking, adds a forced detour, then introduces moving hazards and rescue urgency. The player switches between manual and Jev control at the current state and can restore a checkpoint into a separate branch.
simulation.jevsRole: Choose a typed recovery, return or hold goal from legal mission targets using user instructions and priorities. Preserve the original six-direction task as a separate benchmark.
simulation.codeRole: Own fixed simulation ticks, movement/velocity, path execution, collision, oxygen, cargo, docking, mission progression, controller authority, checkpoint state and deadline fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: An injected five-second provider delay does not stop world ticks, hazards or oxygen; expired and wrong-branch responses never apply.
Controller transfer preserves world state and manual input takes effect by the next simulation tick.
Every campaign mission has an independently verified reachable win; evaluation truncation differs from hull or oxygen loss.
Checkpoint replay reproduces state hashes and branch histories remain independent without replayed network side effects.
Dock target, collision proxy, compass and altitude match canonical coordinates; keyboard/touch navigation works without the inspector.
All three missions can be completed manually; model assistance is evaluated on mission priorities separately from code route planning.

evaluation.design: Freeze 20 development worlds and 150 test worlds, 50 each for easy collection, forced detours and competing core orders. Verify distinct hazards and solvability independently. Run three repeats in geometry-only and assisted-observation conditions, 900 Jev episodes and at most 63,000 logical decisions. Report paired seed-clustered uncertainty, fixed versions and option-order effects. For new real-time play, first test 1,000 local delayed-response/handoff/restore schedules, then 30 held-out three-mission campaigns with three Jev repeats and at most 20 goals per mission, 5,400 logical decisions. Keep game versions and provider failures separate.
baselines: Shortest safe path to nearest core
Independent exact no-damage collect-all-and-return search over position and core mask
For real-time play: manual control and code-only autopilot
metrics: Independent completion, cores returned, remaining hull, collision/boundary count and action count
Excess moves over the constrained oracle and repeated-state loops
Win numerator/denominator, difficulty strata and paired seed-clustered intervals
Physical request wall/service latency, retry/failure count, actual cost and decision deadline misses
For real-time play: campaign completion, rescue-priority adherence, mission time, fallback time, stale applications and takeover latency

coverage.current: Six published episodes on seeds 7,19,42, three Jev and three greedy; 96 Jev actions; both win 3/3; no unsafe immediate alternatives encountered. Audit-only code probes add 1,000 greedy seeds and a crafted detour/docking check, not Jev evidence.
coverage.full: No external split exists. Proposed full declared grid set is 150 held-out worlds across three challenge strata, tested with two observation conditions and three repeats.
coverage.feasibility: Exact no-damage search has at most 1,014 positions times eight core masks for current rules. Local baseline and lifecycle checks are cheap. New Jev runs require an explicit request budget and a physical-request ledger; no new model calls were made.

libraries.name: Three.js OrbitControls
libraries.use: Use existing camera angles and reset/save controls for a compass and repeatable training view; Jev remains responsible for mission goals.

libraries.name: Rapier scene queries
libraries.use: Optional future continuous-flight shape casts and collision proxies; unnecessary for the preserved integer-grid benchmark.

libraries.name: XState persistence
libraries.use: Persist mission/control phases alongside world snapshots; restore with a new request generation and explicit ownership.
